The '''Spanish Glossary''' is a bilingual (Spanish–English) vocabulary reference in the [[The Library of Ashurbanipal|Library of Ashurbanipal]]'s [[Glossaries]] section — a companion to the [[Crypto Glossary]] and the [[Psychedelic and Psychopharmacology Glossary]]. It collects roughly 850 everyday Spanish words and their English meanings, grouped by theme (days, numbers, colors, food, verbs, people, places, and more) so a reader can build a working foundation for reading, speaking, and understanding Spanish. Each entry lists the '''Spanish''' term first, followed by its English translation; regional variants are shown with a slash (/), and gender or usage notes are given in parentheses where helpful.

* '''otra vez / de nuevo''' — again

== Question Words — Palabras Interrogativas ==

* '''quién / quiénes''' — who (''quiénes'' plural)
* '''qué''' — what
* '''cuándo''' — when
* '''dónde''' — where
* '''por qué''' — why
* '''cómo''' — how
* '''cuál / cuáles''' — which (''cuáles'' plural)
* '''cuánto/a''' — how much
* '''cuántos/as''' — how many
* '''de quién''' — whose

== Pronunciation Notes ==

* The '''ll''' (as in ''amarillo'' or ''calle'') sounds like a "y" in most of Latin America, not the "ly" sound sometimes heard in Spain.
* The '''j''' sounds like an English "h" — so ''rojo'' sounds like "roho".
* The letter '''h''' is always silent — ''hombre'' sounds like "ombre".
* '''ñ''' (as in ''mañana'' or ''español'') makes the "ny" sound, like the middle of "canyon".
* '''agua''' is feminine (''el agua'') but takes ''el'' because it begins with a stressed "a" — it stays feminine, so cold water is ''agua fría''.
